rows.verified: Landlords must maintain gas pipework, appliances and flues that they own and provide for tenants.
Covered gas appliances and flues require a safety check every 12 months by a Gas Safe registered engineer.
Permanent and portable gas appliances and associated flues provided by the landlord fall within annual check duties.
Gas installation, maintenance and safety-check work must be performed by a suitably registered Gas Safe engineer where required.
Existing tenants must receive the latest gas safety record within 28 days of the completed check.
New tenants must receive the current gas safety record before moving in.
The record identifies appliances and flues, engineer details, check date, property and landlord, defects and remedial actions.
Gas safety records must be retained until two further checks have been completed.
Electronic records are acceptable when reproducible, protected from loss or interference and able to identify the engineer.
Safety defects must be corrected promptly and a suspected unsafe appliance must not be used until remedied.
Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas that can be produced when combustion appliances or flues are unsafe or poorly ventilated.
Carbon monoxide can be produced by appliances burning gas, oil, wood, coal and other fossil fuels.
Possible symptoms include headache, dizziness, nausea, tiredness, breathlessness, chest or stomach pain, visual problems, erratic behaviour and loss of consciousness.
Early carbon-monoxide symptoms can resemble flu, viral illness, food poisoning or tiredness.
Suspected appliance leakage guidance includes switching off the appliance, shutting the gas supply, ventilating rooms and seeking urgent medical advice.
Suspected gas or carbon-monoxide emergencies are directed to the National Gas Emergency Service.
Air inlets, ventilation, flues and chimneys must remain suitable and unobstructed for safe combustion.
In England relevant landlords must provide a carbon-monoxide alarm in living accommodation containing a fixed combustion appliance, excluding gas cookers.
An annual gas safety check is not assumed to replace effective ongoing maintenance or necessary remedial work.
Gas duties and carbon-monoxide controls depend on installed appliances, occupancy and maintenance and are not inherent parcel-level risk scores.
